newsitem.title: USA: Perot files suit to get into U.S. campaign debates.
newsitem.headline: Perot files suit to get into U.S. campaign debates.

text.p: Reform Party presidential nominee Ross Perot filed suit on Monday demanding that Perot be allowed to join in campaign debates between President Bill Clinton and Republican Bob Dole in October.

Lawyers representing Perot and his running mate, economist Pat Choate, filed suit in U.S. District Court in Washington demanding that the two be brought into scheduled candidates' debates despite the decision of a debates commission and the two major candidates' campaigns to exclude them.

"We are here this morning because there is no more fundamental exercise of free speech in this country than the right to vote for the candidate of your choice," Perot campaign spokesman Russell Verney told reporters at the court house. He said a Louis Harris poll found that 76 percent of voters want Perot included in the debates as he was in 1992.

Perot's suit named the Federal Election Commission, which oversees campaign financing laws but has not been involved in debate preparations, as the agency it wants to be directed to have the Reform Party candidates included.

The scheduled presidential debates -- set for October 6 and 16, with a vice presidential contest on October 9 -- were basically organised by a private, bipartisan presidential debates commission and approved by the Clinton and Dole campaigns. But Perot's lawsuit said he regards the commission as fraudulent and its debate decision as illegal.

The commission recommended last week that Perot, who won 19 percent of the 1992 presidential popular vote, should not be invited this time because it felt he had no realistic chance of winning. Clinton's camp originally supported Perot's demand to be included but gave up that position last weekend in agreeing on debate terms with the Dole camp, which opposed Perot's participation.
